current_formulation: RFC 5322 requires one globally unique Message-ID per message version and allows only one written form of it; older forms are parsed only.

steps.formulation: RFC 733 gives each version of a message a unique identifier, guaranteed by the host that generates it, and allows one Message-ID field per message.
steps.quote: This field contains a unique identifier (the phrase) which refers to THIS version of THIS message.

steps.formulation: RFC 822 keeps the meaning and writes the identifier in address form inside angle brackets.
steps.quote: This field contains a unique identifier (the local-part address unit) which refers to THIS version of THIS message.

criticism.quote: especially since Message-IDs and email addresses have identical syntax.

steps.formulation: RFC 1036 forbids reuse of an identifier during the lifetime of an earlier message and treats foreign identifiers as opaque strings.
steps.quote: The Message-ID may not be reused during the lifetime of any previous message with the same Message-ID.

steps.formulation: RFC 2822 requires global uniqueness and lets the sender's intent decide whether a changed message keeps its identifier.
steps.quote: The message identifier (msg-id) itself MUST be a globally unique identifier for a message.

criticism.quote: The actual text in RFC 2822 may use quoting, resulting in multiple ways of expressing the same Message ID.

steps.formulation: RFC 5322 allows only the dot-atom form on the left-hand side and no internal whitespace, so one identifier has one written form.
steps.quote: this syntax only permits the dot-atom-text form on the left-hand side
